messages:
Ivy: New hire ran our interactive onboarding CLI (rw onboarding) and hit an auth snag I wanted to capture.
Ken: what did they do?
Ivy: They picked the KMS-backed key flow during the wizard (we show: 1) paste API key, 2) point to KMS id, 3) ephemeral token). They chose KMS id and the sampleapp runtime failed with "unsupported credential type" on start.
Omar: Hmm our sampleapp runtime expects a plaintext API key in env (REDWOOD_API_KEY). KMS flow is supported only in Dedicated/private deployments via our agent; we never wired the local sampleapp to call the KMS helper.
Ivy: Repro steps I used:
```
# onboarding
rw onboarding --kms-id projects/teams/keys/abc123
# CLI writes env: REDWOOD_KMS_KEY_ID=projects/teams/keys/abc123
./scripts/dev-local -> runtime errors with "unsupported credential type: kms"
```
Ken: Oof. The interactive wizard writing REDWOOD_KMS_KEY_ID without warning the user that local sampleapp doesn't support it is bad DX. New hires assume onboarding puts them in a working state.
Omar: Two axes here: (1) fix the onboarding wizard to prefer a plaintext API key for local dev and document KMS flow is for deployed infra, (2) make sampleapp detect REDWOOD_KMS_KEY_ID and show a friendly message suggesting using ephemeral token or plaintext key for local testing.
Ivy: Also noticed the wizard set both REDWOOD_API_KEY and REDWOOD_KMS_KEY_ID in one case (they manually pasted a key then picked KMS). That created precedence confusion in the runtime: it picked REDWOOD_KMS_KEY_ID but then couldn't use it.
authbot: FYI legacy alias behavior: if multiple auth envs present, precedence order is: REDWOOD_API_KEY > REDWOOD_KEY > REDWOOD_KMS_KEY_ID (deprecated ordering). This will soon be normalized.
Ken: Suggested quick fixes:
- Change rw onboarding default for local flow to ask: "Use plaintext API key for local dev? [Y/n]" and only write REDWOOD_API_KEY unless user explicitly opts into KMS for deployed infra.
- Sampleapp: on startup detect unsupported credential types (KMS id when no agent present) and print a non-fatal hint: "Detected KMS-managed key; local runtime cannot use KMS directly. Use rw auth:ephemeral or set REDWOOD_API_KEY for testing."
- Add a small cmd `rw auth:doctor` that prints which credential will be used and any mismatches (without exposing secrets).
Omar: Longer term: implement a KMS shim in the local dev agent that can exchange KMS ids for ephemeral tokens for devs, behind a flag. Also add cross-SDK tests for KMS vs plaintext env precedence.
Ivy: Can we also update the onboarding UX to not write multiple auth envs simultaneously? The wizard should fail more loudly if a user tries to configure conflicting creds.
Ken: I'll draft the onboarding change and sampleapp startup hint. Omar will handle the `auth:doctor` CLI.
Docs: I'll file a docs ticket to update onboarding docs, and add a short note in quickstart about KMS vs plaintext key flows.
authbot: Created ticket DEVX-9012: "onboarding wizard writes KMS env without local runtime support; add startup hint + auth:doctor" at 3623456816.
Ivy: Thanks team. Small UX fixes here will avoid a lot of confused new hires.
Ken: PR opened for onboarding change: https://git.example/redwood/cli/pull/1299 (adds prompt + safer defaults).
Omar: Will follow up with PR for auth:doctor and sampleapp startup hint.
Docs: Filed DOCS-921: "Onboarding: KMS vs API key local dev guidance" referencing DEVX-9012.
Ivy: Will validate once PRs land.
